items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Kurt Bloom was playing the other tenor

ctx.x: Well, let's see. Tiny -- well, Cliff Leeman was there for a while, but then Tiny Kahn took over on the drums, a beautiful man, left us very prematurely. And Eddie Safranski was playing bass, and Carlos Vidal had the bongos and the conga, mostly conga. And Claude Williamson was the piano player. And we had, let's see, Obie Masingill, Dick Kenney -- the other couple of trombone players escape

me. Let's see, there was Lenny something playing the alto saxophone player. Dick Hayfer, tenor. Dave Matthews, tenor. No, Dick Hayfer took Dave Matthews place. Kurt Bloom was playing the other tenor, and Reuben Leon, who's now a union official in L.A. Everybody gets old, don't they? Well, that's about it. The trombones -- I can't remember the other two. Oh, Kenny Matlock was one of them, and -- but it was a real -- but I've got to tell you something about that band. As great as that trumpet section was and as…
And, well, that was it. We knocked it off on my birthday, October 26, 1949.
